items.title: Introduction
items.body: Status: approved · Revision: 9 · Owner: Ankur Jain · Describes `main`

items.title: Problem
items.body:
People need to review what an agent writes: decisions, requirements, plans, or any document. Code review has a good interface, but everything else is reviewed as text in a terminal. That review is all or nothing, and it leaves no record. A reviewer can't point at the words they mean, suggest a change, or answer the agent's questions in place. The agent can't read the review back as data, so it rewrites more than it was asked to. Work goes on before the document is approved.

A person also needs to trust a review. They need to know that an approval came from them and not from an agent. They need to know that nothing leaves their machine unless they choose a team review on GitHub. A team needs to review a decision where it already reviews code.

Teams that build with agents need the work around a review too. A change must be kept as it was asked, its documents reviewed in order, and its work tracked with a definition of done. A requester reads the requirements to decide what gets built, so they must read as behavior and not as a code index. People who want to change hoop need a repository that builds and tests on any machine.

items.title: Success criteria
items.body:
| Metric | Baseline | Target | How measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tools an agent sees in a project without devloop. | 13 | 8, with one old name marked. | The tool list of a fresh session. |
| Share of proposed edits that hoop refuses. | The audit report before the edit rules were stated. | Half of that share. | The audit report over a week of use. |
| Ways an agent without a shell can wait for a review. | 0 | 1 | A session with no shell tool. |
| Skipped checks shown as a warning. | 0 | Every one | The submit result and the review page. |
| Approvals marked verified that lack a GitHub sign-in. | Any local request could approve. | 0 | The audit trail of each approved review. |
| Section comments lost when a heading is renamed. | All of them | 0 | A revision that renames a commented heading. |
| Changes listed on a page with their documents. | 0 | Every change in the repository. | The change request page. |
| Tracker items without a definition of done. | The tracker page's flag counts them. | 0 | The tracker page's flag. |
| Steps from a fresh clone to passing tests on another machine. | The tests failed on personal paths. | Install, then test. | A clean checkout in CI. |
| Code findings in the project PRD. | There were 126 code spans, with 88 test file names. | 0 | The writing checker. |
| Change request names in the project HLD and LLD, outside status lines. | 43 and 13 | 0 | The writing checker. |
| Requirements in the project PRD that end with their change requests. | 0 of 73 | Every one | The writing checker reports each one that doesn't. |
| Facts of an old project PRD with no new place after a move. | Not measured | 0 | A script reads the move's fact map. |
| Code findings on the first check of the next three new PRDs. | Not measured | 0 | The check result hoop shows on each first submit. |

items.title: Target personas
items.body:
- **Requester:** The person working with the agent. They ask for a change, review most documents   on the local page, and give the final approval.
- **Reviewer:** A teammate asked to weigh in, who comments on the local page or on a GitHub pull   request.
- **Author agent:** Claude or any MCP client that submits a document, waits, reads feedback,   replies and proposes edits.
- **devloop agents:** The owner agents that write a change's PRD, HLD and LLD, and the persona   agents that review each one before the requester sees it.
- **Contributor:** Someone who clones hoop to change it.
- **Another project's maintainer:** Someone whose project uses devloop, with documents written   under earlier rules.

items.title: Quality bars
items.body:
- NFR-1: Reviews stay on the person's machine. The pages run on 127.0.0.1, in one background process that sessions   and commands start. Nothing leaves the machine except on the GitHub channel and in the GitHub   sign-in for a final approval. The pages refuse a foreign Host, a foreign Origin and writes that   aren't JSON. Acceptance: a write from another site is refused, and a local review sends nothing   to the network until a final approval. Changes: CR-1, CR-22, CR-31.
- NFR-2: Reviewer comments are untrusted input to the agent, and the agent gets them as data.   Acceptance: a comment that holds instructions reaches the agent as a field of the feedback and   runs nothing. Changes: CR-1.
- NFR-3: A 50-item review renders in under a second. It isn't measured yet. Acceptance: a 50-item   review shows in full within one second of opening. Changes: CR-1.
- NFR-4: The review and feedback formats are versioned, as `hoop/review@0` and `hoop/feedback@0`.   A field added to a format keeps its version. Acceptance: every document and every feedback names   its format and version. Changes: CR-1, CR-31.
- NFR-5: The GitHub channel uses the GitHub command line's own login, and the final approval uses a   GitHub sign-in in the browser. hoop stores no token. Acceptance: after a review on each channel,   the person's hoop folder holds no GitHub token. Changes: CR-1, CR-31.
- NFR-6: Rendering and export are deterministic. Acceptance: rendering or exporting the same   revision twice gives identical output. Changes: CR-1.
- NFR-7: The product runs on Node 18.18 or later, with no native dependencies. Acceptance: an install and   the tests pass on Node 18.18. Changes: CR-1.
- NFR-8: Every refusal in FR-27 and FR-28 names the document or pull request, and the command that   fixes it. Acceptance: a refused build step names the document that isn't approved and the   command to run. Changes: CR-3.
- NFR-11: Every page keeps one type scale and one content width. It works in both themes, at 400   pixels wide, from the keyboard and with requests to other hosts blocked. Acceptance: an   automated accessibility check finds no serious problem on any page in those conditions.   Changes: CR-9.
- NFR-12: A 1000-line document renders in under 200 milliseconds. Acceptance: the measured render   time of a 1000-line document stays under 200 milliseconds. Changes: CR-9.
- NFR-13: No request from a page runs a check or waits for one, and no folder path reaches the   page. Acceptance: the review page shows a check's outcome without starting it, and its responses   hold no folder path. Changes: CR-10.
- NFR-14: No request, from a page or from any site, can stop or restart the pages process. Only   requests from hoop's own pages count as use. Acceptance: a request from another site neither   stops the pages nor keeps them running. Changes: CR-22.
- NFR-15: NFR-13 still holds when the pages serve several repositories, and no response holds a   folder path. Acceptance: with two repositories open, no page response holds a folder path.   Changes: CR-22.
- NFR-16: Watching for a newer release adds no more than 50 milliseconds to a page load.   Acceptance: a page loads no more than 50 milliseconds slower with the watch on than with it off.   Changes: CR-22.
- NFR-17: A change keeps every capability users have, unless its PRD names the loss as a change to   current behavior. Acceptance: every current acceptance run passes, with renamed tools called by   their old names. Changes: CR-23, CR-31.
- NFR-18: The change request page, the sign-in states and the audit trail meet NFR-11. Acceptance:   the page checks pass for each of them. Changes: CR-31.
- NFR-19: Diagram support adds no more than 50 milliseconds to the load of a page with no diagram.   Acceptance: the load time of a review without diagrams, with and without diagram support.   Changes: CR-12, CR-31.
- NFR-20: A diagram can never run script, load anything or change the page outside its own box.   Acceptance: a review with a hostile diagram shows no script effect and makes no request.   Changes: CR-12, CR-31.
- NFR-21: The checks on every pull request finish in under ten minutes. The commit check finishes   in under twenty seconds on a typical change. Acceptance: the times of the CI run and the commit   hook on a typical change stay under those limits. Changes: CR-20, CR-31.
- NFR-22: When a project's documents move to new rules, no fact is lost. Each requirement, section   and history phrase of the old PRD gets a named new place. So does each change request name in   the old HLD and LLD. A fact map records each new place. Acceptance: a script finds every mapped   place, every requirement ID in the new PRD or the retired list, and each requirement's tests. Changes: CR-29, CR-30, CR-31.
- NFR-23: The checker's rules report nothing on the project documents and the templates. In a sample   document, they flag each kind FR-108 lists, and each change request name in an HLD or an LLD.   Acceptance: the checker reports zero findings on the first, and one finding for each planted case   in the second. Changes: CR-30, CR-31.
- NFR-24: An author sees the check result on submit with no wait they notice. Acceptance: hoop's   recorded check time for the project PRD stays under one second. Changes: CR-30, CR-31.

items.title: Changes to current behavior
items.body: None. This PRD describes the product as it is on `main`, and each change records what it alters in its own PRD.

items.title: An agent submits a document
items.body:
The agent submits markdown or a decision document, gets a review and its link, and submits each new revision to the same review.

- FR-16: `hoop_submit` shall turn any markdown into a review, with a section for each heading and a   line for each block. Its result carries the outcome of the project's check (FR-42). Acceptance: a   submitted markdown file shows its headings as sections and each paragraph as one line.   Changes: CR-1, CR-10, CR-31.
- FR-1: When an agent submits a valid `hoop/review@0` decision document with   `hoop_submit_decision`, the product shall store it and return a review ID and a link. Given a   review ID, the submit adds a revision instead. Acceptance: a submitted decision document returns   an ID and a link, and a second submit with that ID adds revision 2. Changes: CR-1, CR-31.
- FR-61: `hoop_submit` and `hoop submit` shall take markdown. `hoop_submit_decision` and   `hoop submit-decision` take a decision document. The README says when to use each. Acceptance:   the README's guide names each, and each pair accepts its format. Changes: CR-24, CR-31.
- FR-62: For the next two minor versions, `hoop_submit` shall still accept a decision document, and   the old tool and command names still work. Each old use says the new name, and the changelog   says when the old names go. Acceptance: an old call succeeds, and its result names the new tool.   Changes: CR-24, CR-31.
- FR-63: Each submit result shall state one outcome: created, revised or superseded. It names the   review to use next. Acceptance: a submit against an approved review says superseded and names   the new review. Changes: CR-24, CR-31.
- FR-17: `hoop_export`, and the approval of a document, shall give its markdown back. Unedited text   comes back byte for byte, with any number of blank lines around headings. Acceptance: exporting   an unedited document gives a file identical to the one submitted. Changes: CR-1, CR-2.

items.title: An agent's tools and commands
items.body:
An agent works through MCP tools, and a person or a session without MCP uses the same operations as commands.

- FR-31: Every agent tool shall also be a terminal command with the same input and refusals. The   README's tool table pairs them, such as `hoop submit` for `hoop_submit`. Acceptance: a tool and   its command refuse the same bad input with the same message. Changes: CR-3, CR-31.
- FR-58: In a project without devloop, an agent shall see eight tools. They are `hoop_submit`,   `hoop_submit_decision`, `hoop_feedback`, `hoop_wait`, `hoop_propose_edits`, `hoop_reply`,   `hoop_export`, and the old name `hoop_submit_markdown`, marked as old. Acceptance: a fresh   session in such a project lists exactly these. Changes: CR-23, CR-24, CR-26, CR-31.
- FR-59: When a project turns devloop on in its `hoop.config.json`, an agent shall also see more.   It sees the change request and tracker tools, and the change argument on submit. devloop's setup   turns it on. Acceptance: the same session lists fifteen tools after the setting. Changes: CR-23,   CR-31.
- FR-141: A project that already holds change requests shall keep devloop's tools without the   setting. Acceptance: hoop's own repository, with no new setting, lists all fifteen tools.   Changes: CR-23, CR-31.
- FR-60: Every terminal command shall keep working whatever the setting. The help lists devloop's   commands in their own group. Acceptance: `hoop help` shows two groups, and each devloop command   runs in a project without the setting. Changes: CR-23, CR-31.

items.title: An agent waits for a review and reads it
items.body:
The agent waits for a reviewer, reads the feedback as data, replies in threads and revises.

- FR-66: `hoop_wait` shall hold until a review arrives on the latest revision, or the review is   approved or closed. It holds at most 45 seconds, then says to call again. Acceptance: an agent   with no shell gets a reviewer's comments through `hoop_wait` alone. Changes: CR-26, CR-31.
- FR-8: `hoop wait` shall exit and print the feedback when a review arrives on the latest revision,   or the review is approved or closed. It retries a brief error, such as a dropped connection.   Acceptance: a wait that runs in the background prints the reviewer's comments once the reviewer   finishes. Changes: CR-1.
- FR-67: `hoop wait` in the background shall keep working as FR-8 says. Acceptance: the wait   behavior of FR-8 passes unchanged. Changes: CR-26, CR-31.
- FR-5: `hoop_feedback` shall return pending, or the feedback on the latest revision. The feedback   includes what was applied and the status of each proposed edit. Acceptance: after a review, the   feedback lists its comments, its applied suggestions and each edit's status. Changes: CR-1.
- FR-64: Reading feedback for a superseded review shall point to the review that replaced it.   Acceptance: the feedback of the old review names the new one. Changes: CR-24, CR-31.
- FR-11: `hoop_reply` shall add the agent's reply to a thread, on the local page or on GitHub.   Acceptance: the reply shows in its thread on both channels. Changes: CR-1.

items.title: A reviewer reviews on the local page
items.body:
The reviewer opens the link, reads the document, comments, and finishes with a verdict.

- FR-3: The review page shall show the TL;DR, then numbered lines grouped into items, an outline   and a Viewed toggle for each item. The outline is a tree of nested sections. An automatic TL;DR   that repeats the first paragraph shows once, as that paragraph (FR-39). Acceptance: a review   shows its TL;DR, numbered lines, a nested outline and a Viewed toggle on each item.   Changes: CR-1, CR-9, CR-31.
- FR-4: A reviewer shall comment on a whole line or on selected text, attach suggested text, answer   questions and keep comments pending. They finish with Comment, Approve or Request changes.   Approve and Request changes count as the person's own only with a GitHub sign-in (FR-81).   Acceptance: a reviewer leaves a pending comment and a suggestion, then sends both with a verdict.   Changes: CR-1, CR-31.
- FR-4a: Commented text shall stay highlighted, except while comments are hidden (FR-46). Typed   words in "Only about this text" anchor a comment without a mouse. Acceptance: a comment made from   the keyboard on typed words highlights those words. Changes: CR-1, CR-13.
- FR-19: A comment on a heading shall cover its section and every section nested in it. A comment   on the title or the TL;DR covers the whole document. Acceptance: the feedback gives a heading   comment's scope as its sections, and a title comment's scope as the document. Changes: CR-1,   CR-31.
- FR-6: A new revision shall offer "Changes since rev N" and keep earlier threads. It marks threads   on changed lines as outdated, and reviewers can resolve them. A resolved thread shows as a summary   row (FR-45). Acceptance: after a revision changes a commented line, its thread shows as outdated   and can be resolved. Changes: CR-1, CR-13.
- FR-7: A final approval shall freeze the revision, and a later submit starts a review that   supersedes it. An agent approval doesn't freeze it (FR-82). Acceptance: after a final approval   the review refuses comments, and a new submit names the review it supersedes. Changes: CR-1,   CR-31.
- FR-10: Approving a local review shall write `decisions/<slug>.json` and `decisions/<slug>.md` to   the repository it came from. Acceptance: after the approval, both files are in that repository.   Changes: CR-1.
- FR-65: After an approval, the files it wrote shall show on the review page and in the command's   output. Acceptance: an approved review's page lists the decision files. Changes: CR-24, CR-31.

items.title: A reviewer reads a structured document
items.body:
The reviewer reads nested sections, tables and diagrams as the author wrote them, across revisions.

- FR-76: A document's sections shall nest up to five levels under its title. The outline is a tree   that expands and collapses, and each section sits inside its parent. Acceptance: a document with   six heading levels shows five nested levels under the title. Changes: CR-12, CR-31.
- FR-77: A comment on a heading shall cover its section and every section nested in it.   Acceptance: the comment's scope lists the nested sections. Changes: CR-12, CR-31.
- FR-78: A section shall keep its comments when its heading is renamed in a new revision. It keeps   them when it stays at the same level, under the same parent, in the same place among its   siblings. Two sections with the same heading keep their own comments. Acceptance: after a rename,   the comments still show on that section. Changes: CR-12, CR-31.
- FR-142: Reviews stored by earlier releases shall keep every comment on its section. Acceptance: a   review stored by an earlier release opens with all its comments in place. Changes: CR-12, CR-31.
- FR-79: A markdown table on a review page shall show as a table, with its header row and its   columns aligned. Each row stays one line to comment on. Acceptance: a review of a table shows a   header row, and a comment on a row stays on that row. Changes: CR-6, CR-12, CR-31.
- FR-80: A Mermaid diagram shall show as a drawn diagram on every page, without reaching another   host. A reviewer comments on it like a line. Acceptance: a review with a diagram draws it with   other hosts blocked. Changes: CR-6, CR-12, CR-31.

items.title: Every page looks and reads the same
items.body:
Every page shares one frame, one set of status labels and one way to show text and comments.

- FR-32: Every page shall show the same frame. It holds the product name, links to the reviews and   the tracker, and the repository in use. A page names its document's repository (FR-53).   Acceptance: each page shows the frame with those links and its repository. Changes: CR-9, CR-22.
- FR-33: Each status shall have one label, one color and one icon on every page. This covers review   statuses, tracker item statuses and change steps. Acceptance: the same status looks the same on   the review list, the tracker page and the change request page. Changes: CR-9.
- FR-34: The review list shall list only reviews, grouped by status with a count for each group.   Each row names its channel and its repository, and shows a date without seconds. Acceptance: the   review list shows each group's count, and each row's channel, repository and date. Changes: CR-9,   CR-22.
- FR-35: Lines shall show markdown as formatted text, with no markdown characters. A table shows as   a table (FR-79), and a tracker's description block shows as written. Acceptance: a line with bold   and a link shows formatted, with no asterisks or brackets. Changes: CR-9, CR-31.
- FR-36: A comment on selected text shall anchor to the source text. A selection inside formatted   text covers the whole formatted run. Acceptance: a selection inside a link anchors the comment to   the link's whole source text. Changes: CR-9.
- FR-37: Typed words in "Only about this text" shall match the shown text, across formatting.   Acceptance: typed words that span bold and plain text anchor the comment. Changes: CR-9.
- FR-38: The comment button shall sit in a gutter and never move the text. Acceptance: hovering a   line shows the button without moving any word. Changes: CR-9.
- FR-39: A document shall hide its section IDs, and labels shall name a section by its title. An   automatic TL;DR shows once, and its earlier comments show under the title. Acceptance: no label   shows a section ID, and an automatic TL;DR shows once. Changes: CR-9.

items.title: Conversations and hidden comments
items.body:
The reviewer collapses settled conversations, and can hide every comment to read the document alone.

- FR-45: A resolved conversation shall show as a summary row with its place and count, until the   reviewer opens it. Resolving a thread collapses it at once, and unresolving shows it in full. A   local thread with a reply after its resolution shows in full again. A GitHub thread follows   GitHub's resolved state. Acceptance: resolving a thread turns it into a summary row at once.   Changes: CR-13.
- FR-46: One control shall hide every conversation, pending comment, tracked change card and   inserted word, without removing any of the document's own words. Its label counts what it hides,   as "Show comments (N)". Acceptance: with comments hidden, the page shows only the document's own   words. Changes: CR-13.
- FR-47: Comments shall show whenever the reviewer writes a comment or reaches a verdict, and on   every new visit. Acceptance: a new visit to a page where comments were hidden shows them.   Changes: CR-13.

items.title: Comments become edits
items.body:
A reviewer applies a suggestion, or the agent proposes small edits that the reviewer accepts as tracked changes.

- FR-18: A reviewer shall Apply an exact suggestion. Only that span changes, in a new revision, and   the thread is marked applied. Acceptance: after Apply, the new revision differs from the old one   only in the suggested span. Changes: CR-1.
- FR-74: A reviewer shall delete selected text within a line in one action, as a suggestion.   Acceptance: the delete shows as a suggestion that Apply removes. Changes: CR-25, CR-31.
- FR-75: A reviewer shall edit a line in place, as a suggestion. Acceptance: the edited line shows   as a suggestion with Apply. Changes: CR-25, CR-31.
- FR-71: A comment, a reply or a proposed edit shall be able to name the exact words it covers in   place of a line number. The words match the line's text as feedback shows it. An item may narrow   the search. Acceptance: an agent comments by quote alone, and the comment sits on the right line.   Changes: CR-25, CR-31.
- FR-72: Feedback shall state each comment's edit scope: the line, the section or the whole   document. Acceptance: each comment in the feedback names its scope. Changes: CR-25, CR-31.
- FR-20: `hoop_propose_edits` shall take span edits for a thread. Each edit's search text occurs   once in its line, inside the thread's scope, which covers nested sections. The commented text   must read as it did when the comment was made. Otherwise the call is refused with an error for   each field. Acceptance: an edit whose search text occurs twice in its line is refused, and the   error names that edit. Changes: CR-1, CR-31.
- FR-73: The proposed edits tool shall state every edit rule in its description. Each refusal names   the rule it broke. Acceptance: a refused edit names its rule, and the description lists all   rules. Changes: CR-25, CR-31.
- FR-21: Proposed edits shall show inline as tracked changes with Accept and Reject. Accepting   applies only that span, and only while the line reads exactly as when proposed. Acceptance:   accepting an edit changes only its span, and an edit on a line that changed can't be accepted.   Changes: CR-1.
- FR-22: Text outside an applied span shall stay byte for byte the same. In documents, an edit   can't change the markdown structure or empty a line. An edit over half a line is flagged as a   large rewrite. Acceptance: an edit that would turn a paragraph into a heading is refused.   Changes: CR-1.

items.title: Agents comment, and the requester approves
items.body:
Agents review with comments, and only the signed-in person gives the final approval.

- FR-81: A verdict without a GitHub sign-in shall count as an agent's. An approve becomes an agent   approval, and a request for changes becomes a comment. The result says so. Acceptance: an approve   sent without a sign-in leaves the review open. Changes: CR-14, CR-31.
- FR-82: An agent approval shall be recorded on the review and never freeze it. Acceptance: after an   agent approval, the review still takes comments. Changes: CR-14, CR-31.
- FR-83: The final approval of a local review shall need the person's GitHub sign-in in the   browser. The page shows a code, the person confirms it on GitHub, and the approval records their   login. Acceptance: an approval after the sign-in shows the login. Changes: CR-14, CR-31.
- FR-143: A sign-in shall last eight hours, in that browser only. Each final approval is still a   click on that review's page. Acceptance: a request from outside that browser can't use the   sign-in. Changes: CR-14, CR-31.
- FR-84: A person shall be able to turn the sign-in off in their own settings, but no repository   can. Every approval made without a sign-in is marked unverified on the page, in the audit trail   and in the decision record. Acceptance: with the setting off, an approval works and shows as   unverified. Changes: CR-14, CR-31.
- FR-144: A person shall be able to set their own GitHub OAuth App in their own settings, in place   of hoop's. Acceptance: a sign-in with a person's own app records the login. Changes: CR-14,   CR-31.
- FR-85: An approval shall be able to carry notes. The decision record and the feedback keep them.   Acceptance: a note written with an approval shows in the decision record. Changes: CR-14, CR-31.
- FR-86: Each review page shall show its audit trail. It lists every comment, agent approval and   final approval, with who and when. Acceptance: the trail of an approved review lists each event.   Changes: CR-14, CR-31.
- FR-87: When an agent in Claude Code leaves plan mode, a hook shall open its plan for review in   hoop. The agent goes on only after the final approval, and gets the feedback otherwise. The person   turns the hook on. Acceptance: with the hook on, a plan waits for approval in hoop. Changes:   CR-14, CR-31.
- FR-145: When the plan hook's wait ends before a verdict, the agent shall stop. It is told the   review's link and to wait for the person. Acceptance: a plan with no verdict stops the agent with   that message. Changes: CR-14, CR-31.

items.title: A team reviews on GitHub
items.body:
The agent submits on the GitHub channel, the team reviews the pull request, and merging decides.

- FR-12: On the GitHub channel, submitting shall open a pull request. It holds   `decisions/<slug>.json`, the rendered `decisions/<slug>.md`, and a description with the TL;DR   and a checkbox for each question. Acceptance: the new pull request shows both files and a   checkbox for each question. Changes: CR-1.
- FR-13: `hoop_feedback` shall read the pull request's reviews into the same feedback document. It   reads line comments mapped to item and line, suggestions, replies, ticked answers and resolved   threads. Comments off item lines go into the summary. Acceptance: a GitHub line comment shows in   the feedback on its item and line. Changes: CR-1.
- FR-14: A revision of a GitHub review shall be a new commit on the same pull request, and ticked   answers stay ticked. Acceptance: after a revision, the pull request has one more commit and the   same ticked answers. Changes: CR-1.
- FR-15: Merging the pull request shall approve the review, and closing it unmerged rejects it.   Acceptance: after a close without a merge, the feedback says the review is closed. Changes: CR-1.

items.title: A project checks its documents on submit
items.body:
A project names a check command, the person allows it once, and each markdown submit shows the check's findings.

- FR-41: A markdown submission shall run the project's check command, set in `hoop.config.json`.   It runs only when the person's own `~/.hoop/config.json` allows that exact command for that   folder. A decision document, or a repository without a command, runs nothing and returns no   check result. Acceptance: an allowed command runs on a markdown submit and not on a decision   submit. Changes: CR-10.
- FR-42: The submit result shall carry the check's outcome: whether it ran, the command, and each   finding with its source line, its message and its place. The outcome is kept with the revision on   both channels. Acceptance: a submit with one finding returns that finding's line and message.   Changes: CR-10.
- FR-44: The review page shall show the latest checked revision's findings in a panel, and jump to   each finding's line. It names the checked revision, and says when a newer one wasn't checked. The   GitHub channel has no panel. Acceptance: choosing a finding in the panel moves to its line.   Changes: CR-10.
- FR-68: When a declared check didn't run, the submit result shall lead with a warning that says   why and how to allow it. Acceptance: a submit with a check that isn't allowed starts its result   with that warning. Changes: CR-27, CR-31.
- FR-69: The review page shall show a skipped check as a warning, and say which command to run to   allow it. It shows no folder path. Acceptance: the page names the command and no path. Changes:   CR-27, CR-31.
- FR-70: `hoop allow-check` shall show the exact command a repository declares and ask the person   to confirm. Then it adds the allow entry to the person's own settings. Acceptance: after the   person confirms, the next submit runs the check. Changes: CR-27, CR-31.

items.title: The pages server
items.body:
Sessions and commands share one pages server on a fixed address, which keeps itself current.

- FR-48: Every page shall be served on the usual address, port 4747 or the port the person sets.   Every link from a tool or a command uses it. Acceptance: links from two sessions open on the same   address. Changes: CR-22.
- FR-49: When a session or a command that gives a link finds no hoop server on the usual address,   it shall start one background pages process. That process outlives every session. A session for   the same store uses the one that answers. The check waits at most one second. Acceptance: the   pages still answer after the session that started them ends. Changes: CR-22.
- FR-51: When the pages process is out of date, it shall restart itself into the current code on   the same address, so drafts stay. It is out of date when a live session's install holds a newer   release, or when its own files changed. It tries once for each change. If the new code can't   serve, the old process serves again. Acceptance: after an update, the page shows the new release   and keeps a draft comment. Changes: CR-22.
- FR-53: A review page shall name its review's repository. The tracker page offers the tracker of   each repository with a live session. Acceptance: with sessions in two repositories, the tracker   page offers both trackers. Changes: CR-22.
- FR-54: The frame shall show the hoop release and a short code ID that serve the pages.   Acceptance: the frame shows the release and code ID of the running pages. Changes: CR-22.
- FR-57: The pages process shall stop after an hour with no live session and no request from a   page. An open page counts as use. Acceptance: with no session and no open page, the pages stop   after an hour. Changes: CR-22.

items.title: The improvement loop
items.body:
The maintainer reads where agents and reviewers fail, before changing tools or edit rules.

- FR-23: Every action, every failed tool call and every failed reviewer action shall be recorded in   an audit log on the person's machine. A setting turns the log off. Acceptance: a refused tool call   shows among the failures that `hoop audit` reports. Changes: CR-1.
- FR-24: `hoop audit` shall summarize time to verdict, revisions, edit acceptance, large rewrites and   the top failures. It also counts checks run, findings, and checks that didn't run. Acceptance:   after a week of use, the summary shows each of these. Changes: CR-1, CR-10.

items.title: A team tracks changes and work
items.body:
With devloop, a request becomes a change with its documents, its steps and its tracker.

- FR-25: A change request shall be kept exactly as written, numbered CR-<n>, and shown on the change   request page at intake. Acceptance: a captured request shows on the change request page with its   number and its words unchanged. Changes: CR-3, CR-31.
- FR-26: Each change shall be classified as epic, story, task or bug, with a reason. A corrected type   is recorded with why, in a classification file in `docs/changes/`. Acceptance: a reclassified   change shows its new type and the reason in that file. Changes: CR-3.
- FR-27: A change's PRD, HLD and LLD reviews shall open only in that order, each after the one   before is approved. A re-approved earlier document makes the later ones need approval again.   Acceptance: opening an HLD review before its PRD is approved is refused. Changes: CR-3.
- FR-28: A change's steps shall be recorded in order, with the time and the actor. The steps are   intake, PRD, HLD, LLD, plan, build, review, accept, merge, fold, or closed. Build needs all three   documents approved and current, and fold needs every linked pull request merged. Acceptance: a   build step before the LLD is approved is refused. Changes: CR-3.
- FR-29: The tracker shall hold epics, stories, tasks, sub-tasks and bugs as a tree. hoop changes   only the cells and rows it is asked to, and refuses if the file changed underneath. Acceptance: a   change to a row after the file was edited elsewhere is refused. Changes: CR-3.
- FR-30: The tracker page (`/tracker`) shall show a repository's trackers as a tree table that   expands, collapses and filters by type and status. It offers each open repository's trackers   (FR-53), and holds no change request rows (FR-93). A tracker under review shows the same tree   with rows to comment on. Acceptance: filtering by status hides the other rows and keeps their   parents. Changes: CR-3, CR-22, CR-31.
- NFR-9: Trackers and changes written by earlier releases still load. Acceptance: a tracker written   before change requests existed opens on the tracker page. Changes: CR-3.
- FR-88: The tracker page shall show an item's description and definition of done when the item is   opened. A checklist shows how many of its points are met. Acceptance: an opened item shows its   block and its count. Changes: CR-11, CR-31.
- FR-89: The tracker page shall flag each item that has no description or no definition of done.   Acceptance: an item without a block is flagged. Changes: CR-11, CR-31.
- FR-90: Each tracker item that hoop adds shall come with a block to fill in. Acceptance: a new row   has a matching block. Changes: CR-11, CR-31.
- FR-91: The project's own tracker shall follow the tracker standard, with a block for every item.   Acceptance: the tracker page flags nothing on hoop's tracker. Changes: CR-5, CR-11, CR-31.
- FR-92: A change request page shall list every change, grouped as queued, in progress, done and   closed. Each change links to its request, its documents, its reviews and its pull requests.   Acceptance: every change in the repository shows with its links. Changes: CR-16, CR-31.
- FR-93: Change requests shall stay out of the tracker. A tracker's root work item points to its   change. Acceptance: the tracker holds no change request rows, and each root item links its   change. Changes: CR-16, CR-31.
- FR-94: Each change's capture and pick-up checks, and each merge, split or drop, shall be recorded   as a revision of its request. The change request page shows them. Acceptance: a merged change   shows the revision that records the merge. Changes: CR-15, CR-16, CR-31.
- FR-95: A change shall be flagged, with a proposal to split it, when its tracker's estimates total   more than 50 files or 2,500 changed lines. That is five pull requests at devloop's limit. The   requester can keep it whole, and the flag records that choice. Acceptance: a change over the   limit shows the flag, and the requester's choice once made. Changes: CR-16, CR-31.
- FR-96: Every change and every tracker item shall have a project, and every change a kind,   functional or non-functional. Existing ones get theirs. Acceptance: every change and item shows   its project. Changes: CR-7, CR-31.
- FR-97: The review list, the change request page and the tracker page shall filter by project.   Acceptance: a filter shows only that project's reviews, changes and items. Changes: CR-7, CR-17,   CR-31.
- FR-98: A person shall move a queued change to another project. A change in progress can't move,   and the refusal says why. Acceptance: a moved change shows under its new project. Changes: CR-7,   CR-17, CR-31.

items.title: Authors write change documents
items.body:
The author starts from a template, writes the document, runs the checker, and submits it to hoop. The reviewers comment, and the requester approves it. When a change merges, its documents fold into the project's own.

- FR-99: When an author starts a PRD, the template shall give five sections in this order. They are   overview and objectives, user interactions and flows, UI states and transitions, edge cases and   error handling, and out of scope. Acceptance: for each section, the template lists what it   contains and what it never holds. Changes: CR-30, CR-31.
- FR-100: The template shall say where the rest of a PRD sits. A quality bar for the whole product   goes in section 1, and one for a single flow sits with that flow. Changed current behavior goes   in section 1, and assumptions and open questions close section 5. Acceptance: the template has a   place for each, and this PRD uses them. Changes: CR-30, CR-31.
- FR-101: When a section doesn't apply to a change, the PRD shall say "None" and give one sentence   why. Acceptance: a PRD for a change with no screens says so under UI states. Changes: CR-30,   CR-31.
- FR-102: The PRD standards shall list the ten things a PRD never holds. The first five are   prescribed implementation details, vague or subjective acceptance criteria, unbounded feature   sets, unvalidated assumptions presented as facts, and hardcoded dates. The other five are finished   visual designs, a missing out of scope section, unlinked dependencies, solutions without problem   statements, and untestable edge cases. Acceptance: the standards name all ten, and a reviewer   comments on each one a PRD holds. Changes: CR-30, CR-31.
- FR-103: A PRD shall name only the public parts that a user or an agent types, reads or sets.   Those are commands, agent tools with their inputs and results, and document formats with their   versions. They also include pages, controls, settings, and files the user edits or reads. It   never names a source or test file, a function, an internal web address, or how data is stored.   Acceptance: the PRD standards state both lists. Changes: CR-30, CR-31.
- FR-104: Each requirement shall have one acceptance sentence that a user or an agent could   observe. It is measurable, and it never names a test. Acceptance: no requirement in a new PRD   names a test, and each one has an acceptance sentence. Changes: CR-30, CR-31.
- FR-105: Each requirement shall end with the change requests that changed its behavior, oldest   first, written as `Changes: CR-3, CR-22`. A change that only rewords it adds nothing. The text   states current behavior, with no history of which change did what. Acceptance: the checker   reports each requirement without the tag. Changes: CR-29, CR-30, CR-31.
- FR-106: An HLD or an LLD shall point only to requirements, by their IDs, and never name a change   request. A change's links to other queued changes live in its notes and the tracker. Acceptance:   the HLD and LLD templates and their review standards state the rule. Changes: CR-29, CR-31.
- FR-107: The LLD's test plan shall name, for each requirement, the tests that prove it. Acceptance:   every requirement in the project PRD has a row in the project LLD's test plan. Changes: CR-30,   CR-31.
- FR-108: In a PRD, the checker shall flag each file path, source or test file name, function call   and web route. It flags them inside code too. Acceptance: a sample PRD gets one finding for each.   Changes: CR-30, CR-31.
- FR-109: The checker shall flag each change request name in an HLD or an LLD, outside its status   line. Acceptance: a sample HLD gets one finding for each name. Changes: CR-29, CR-31.
- FR-110: When a change folds, its requirements shall land in the project PRD with their change   tags. Its design text lands in the project HLD and LLD with no change request names. Acceptance:   the fold steps say so, and the next fold's documents pass the checker. Changes: CR-29, CR-30,   CR-31.
- FR-111: The project PRD shall follow the five sections and every rule above. Every requirement ID   stays, except the retired ones that section 5 lists. Acceptance: the project PRD passes the   checker, and NFR-22's script passes. Changes: CR-30, CR-31.
- FR-112: The project HLD and LLD shall name no change request. Each place that named one points to   the requirements it serves, and a decision keeps its reason. Acceptance: the checker reports no   change request name in either. Changes: CR-29, CR-31.
- FR-113: Before the project PRD moves to the five sections, a comparison shall find the states and   errors that hoop lacks. It compares hoop with GitHub pull request review, Google Docs suggesting   mode and Plannotator. The comparison covers the review page, the review list, the tracker page   and the agent's tools. The gaps become at most one new queued change request for each of those   four. Acceptance: each gap names its change request in the project PRD's open questions.   Changes: CR-30, CR-31.

items.title: A contributor builds hoop
items.body:
A contributor clones the repository, installs, changes the code, and opens a pull request.

- FR-118: The project's tests and scripts shall depend on nothing outside the repository or one   person's machine. A run that needs GitHub takes its repository from a setting, and says so when   it is missing. Acceptance: a clean clone on another machine installs and passes its tests.   Changes: CR-19, CR-20, CR-31.
- FR-119: Installing in a contributor's clone shall set up commit hooks kept in the repository.   Before a commit they run the type check, the linter, the formatter and the writing check on   changed documents. Installing hoop as a tool sets up nothing. Acceptance: a commit with a type   error is refused. Changes: CR-20, CR-31.
- FR-120: The commit check shall refuse a code comment that names a change request or a tracker   item. Acceptance: such a comment is refused, and the whole code base passes. Changes: CR-20,   CR-31.
- FR-121: Before a push, the hooks shall run the tests. Acceptance: a push with a failing test is   refused. Changes: CR-20, CR-31.
- FR-122: Every pull request shall run the type check, the linter and the tests on each supported   Node version, and the browser tests. Acceptance: a pull request shows each check. Changes: CR-20,   CR-31.
- FR-123: The repository shall hold a contributing guide, a code of conduct, a security policy and   a changelog. It also holds issue and pull request templates, editor settings, code owners and   dependency updates. Acceptance: each one is in the repository, and the guide says how to build.   Changes: CR-20, CR-31.
- FR-124: A devloop skill shall check a repository for these practices, and keep them in every   change it drives. Acceptance: the skill reports each missing practice in a repository without   them. Changes: CR-20, CR-31.

items.title: A new user reads the README
items.body:
A new user reads what hoop is, installs it, reviews a first document, and reaches the reference last.

- FR-125: The README shall start with what hoop is, then install and removal, then a short   walkthrough from the reviewer's side. The reference comes last. Acceptance: a reader installs and   reviews a document before reaching the reference. Changes: CR-28, CR-31.
- FR-126: The README shall have a glossary of hoop's terms. Acceptance: it defines materialize,   TL;DR, check, risk, depends on, item types and supersedes. Changes: CR-28, CR-31.
- FR-127: The product shall publish its review and feedback formats as JSON Schema files. The   README's field tables come from the same source. Acceptance: a change to a field changes both.   Changes: CR-28, CR-31.
- FR-128: The README shall show what differs on the GitHub channel, and where the channel is set.   Acceptance: a table lists each difference. Changes: CR-28, CR-31.
- FR-129: The README shall name every side effect, every devloop step, change type and tracker   column, and what two sessions or two repositories do. Acceptance: each is in the README.   Changes: CR-28, CR-31.
- FR-130: The README's tool table and its command examples shall match one to one. Acceptance:   every tool has its command beside it. Changes: CR-28, CR-31.
- FR-131: The README shall say which surfaces may still break, and how a breaking change is   announced in the changelog. It also covers setup for agents other than Claude Code. Acceptance:   the README has a stability section and a setup for one other agent. Changes: CR-28, CR-31.

items.title: 3. UI states and transitions
items.body:
- FR-40: A count badge shall appear only when its count is above zero. Acceptance: an item with no   comments shows no badge. Changes: CR-9.
- FR-52: Every page shall warn while its server is out of date, and name the restart step. That   holds for a foreground `hoop serve` too, which warns but doesn't restart. A page also says when   the pages stopped. Acceptance: a page served by an older release shows the warning and the step.   Changes: CR-22.
- FR-132: The change request page shall show an empty state that says how to capture a change, when   a repository has none. Acceptance: a repository with no changes shows that state. Changes: CR-16,   CR-31.
- FR-133: The sign-in shall show each of its states: the code to enter, waiting, signed in,   expired, denied and offline. Each state says what to do next. Acceptance: each state shows its   next step. Changes: CR-14, CR-31.
- FR-134: A diagram shall show a placeholder while it draws. Acceptance: a slow diagram shows the   placeholder first. Changes: CR-12, CR-31.
- FR-135: An item opened on the tracker page shall show "No definition of done yet" when its block   is missing. Acceptance: such an item shows that text. Changes: CR-11, CR-31.
- FR-114: The writing checker's findings shall show in the review page's check panel like other   findings. Each one names its line and says what to write instead. Acceptance: a PRD that names a   test file shows a finding on that line, which says to move the test to the LLD's test plan.   Changes: CR-30, CR-31.

items.title: 4. Edge cases and error handling
items.body:
- FR-2: When a submitted document is invalid, the product shall reject it with an error for each   field that is wrong. Acceptance: a document with no title is refused, and the error names that   field. Changes: CR-1.
- FR-43: A check shall never stop a submission. Exit 0 means no findings, and exit 1 means   findings. Any other code, a command that can't start, or one that runs past ten seconds means the   check didn't run, and the result says why. Acceptance: a check that runs too long still lets the   submit succeed, and says it didn't run. Changes: CR-10.
- FR-50: When something else holds the usual address, the session's tools shall keep working. That   covers a program that isn't hoop, one that doesn't answer, an older hoop, and a hoop for another   store. Each later call that gives a link checks the address again. Acceptance: with another   program on the port, a submit still succeeds. Changes: CR-22.
- FR-55: A page whose code or data fails to load shall show the error and the restart step in place   of "Loading". Acceptance: a page with data that fails to load shows the error and the step.   Changes: CR-22.
- FR-56: When the pages can't be served, each result that gives a link shall carry a pages notice.   The notice has a status and a message that says why. A command also prints the message on its error   output. That covers another program, another store, an older hoop and a start that fails.   Acceptance: a submit while another program holds the port returns the notice. Changes: CR-22.
- FR-136: When quoted words occur nowhere or more than once, hoop shall refuse the comment or edit.   The refusal shows each place the words occur. Acceptance: an ambiguous quote is refused with its   places. Changes: CR-25, CR-31.
- FR-137: When the sign-in expires, is denied or can't reach GitHub, the approval shall not happen.   The review stays open, and the page says why. Acceptance: an expired code leaves the review open.   Changes: CR-14, CR-31.
- FR-138: When a diagram can't be drawn, its page shall show its source and the reason. Acceptance:   a broken diagram shows its source and an error. Changes: CR-12, CR-31.
- FR-139: When `hoop_wait` ends without a review, its result shall say so and say to call it again.   Acceptance: a wait with no review returns that message within 45 seconds. Changes: CR-26, CR-31.
- FR-140: When a person declines `hoop allow-check`, nothing shall change. Without a terminal, it   refuses and says to run it in one. Acceptance: an agent's call without a terminal is refused.   Changes: CR-27, CR-31.
- FR-115: A PRD whose title names its kind, but without the five sections, shall get one finding on   how to adopt the new shape. It gets no finding for each code name. Acceptance: checking a PRD in   the older shape reports that one finding and no code finding. Changes: CR-30, CR-31.
- FR-116: A project shall list the names its users type that look like code, such as a file the   user edits, in `docs/allowed-names.txt`. The checker never flags a listed name. With no list, it   flags every kind FR-108 names. Acceptance: hoop's PRD names its users' config file and passes   with the list, and gets a finding without it. Changes: CR-30, CR-31.
- FR-117: The checker shall know a PRD, an HLD or an LLD by the kind its title names. It works the   same on the file and on hoop's submit. Acceptance: submitting the project PRD to hoop shows the   same findings as running the checker on its file. Changes: CR-30, CR-31.

The checker never checks a change's request file, which holds the requester's own words.

items.title: 5. Out of scope
items.body:
- Code review of diffs is left out, because GitHub and code review tools cover it.
- Materializing comments on the GitHub channel is left out, because GitHub's Commit suggestion   covers it.
- Accounts, hosting, and notifications beyond GitHub's own are left out.
- A tool to search decisions is left out. People search the `decisions/` folder with grep instead.
- Deleting a whole line in one action is left out. An edit can't empty a line or change a   document's structure, which is a settled rule.
- Pull requests that need a human review on GitHub are left out. The requester dropped them.
- Publishing hoop to npm is left out, and stays an idea in the tracker.
- A sign-in for reviews on the GitHub channel is left out, because merging already needs GitHub.
- Rewriting the documents of past changes is left out. They are frozen records.

items.title: Retired requirements
items.body:
- FR-9 was a tool to search decisions. Its text moved to the out of scope list above.
- NFR-10 stated how the code is built. Its text moved to the HLD's decisions, which point to FR-31   and NFR-4.

items.title: Assumptions and open questions
items.body:
- The product is installed from source. Whether to publish it to npm is still open.
- The project registers its own GitHub OAuth App, and the maintainer creates it once. Its client ID   ships with hoop, and the device sign-in needs no secret.
- 45 seconds is the longest a wait holds, because MCP clients time out a call after 60 seconds.
- The plan review hook ships with hoop, and a person turns it on.
- Every PRD, HLD and LLD names its kind in its title, as the templates show. Documents of past   changes that don't are frozen, so the checker treats them as plain documents.
- A requirement ID never changes, so links from tests and the tracker still work.
- A timing target a user can notice, such as a page that renders in under a second, is a quality   bar. Section 2 excludes internal service targets, not these.
- The requirements of devloop live in hoop's PRD, because devloop ships from this repository.
- A comparison with GitHub pull request review, Google Docs suggesting mode and Plannotator found   seven states and errors that the review page lacks. They are queued as CR-32. The same comparison   found that a person can't close a review on the local page, which touches the review list and the   agent's wait. That gap is queued as CR-33. The tracker page and the agent's tools showed no gap.
